studies.title: At the Table
studies.subtitle: A six-session study for learning to follow Jesus in an ordinary room
studies.summary: Discipleship did not begin in a classroom. It began at tables, on roads, in borrowed rooms. This study is built for the same places: a living room, a kitchen table, a back booth. One person who has walked a little further opens the passage, and the people around the table read, talk, pray, and practice. By the last session, someone at the table is ready to set another one.

studies.title: New at the Table
studies.subtitle: Six sessions for the first weeks of a brand new faith, run around a table by the person who pointed the way
studies.summary: When someone comes to faith, the worst thing we can do is hand them a building and a schedule and walk away. The first weeks decide a great deal. This study is for the believer who led a friend to Jesus, or is walking beside a brand new one, and wants to ground them in the things that hold: who they now are, what the cross actually did, the Spirit who lives in them, how to talk to the Father, how to live on the Word, and how, sooner than they think, they will be the one pointing the way for someone else. It is built for a kitchen table, not a classroom. Keep it slow, keep it warm, and keep it moving outward.
